review_items.rationale: Reviewed artifact 637e0d79cf4444ad8d1a66c0f2bcf0d8 version 1, its fixed plan and harness under direct-checks/c1d4b567efee4cfd958ac3f6356e6964, C_ACCEPTED_LOG_VIEW v1, BIND_STORAGE_VIEW v1, and execution ce685a3cf2234bbca54f8b07081bf7f0. Applicability: the unstable contract explicitly retains in-progress accepted history until Storage queries safely reflect it; the completion contract explains the cross-term replacement hazard. The obligation tests returned logical entry contents, not equality to an internal guard or offset. Entry and ownership: all mutations enter public RawNode methods under serialized driver ownership; private log/unstable access only reads observations. Five nodes start from the same documented storage-backed committed snapshot, then actual campaigns, votes, append rejection/retry and storage-request production create the three-term history. Initial snapshot/HardState assignment is an explicit caller prefix, not assigned critical replacement state. Caller duties: MemoryStorage is the declared no-crash persistence substitute. Each append request writes entries/HardState before responses; requests are FIFO. Node-2 local responses remain FIFO even while already-persisted responses to other recipients progress. Current replacement writes are held in a separate FIFO and all are completed later. No fabricated network or storage-completion messages, membership changes, compaction or snapshot processing occur in the measured interval. Oracle and correlation: replacement serial 4 captures actual accepted work for op=replacement,node=2,entry_index=3, including Index/Term/Type/Data in a deterministic immutable JSON string. Admission serial 8 references serial 4 and independently records a stale MsgStorageAppendResp, pending write and conflicting stored entry. The identity fields do not include term or compared contents. No precondition tests the result log_entry or suppresses an unfavorable result. The result at serial 9 is produced after Step returns and directly queries raftLog.slice; it equals the captured expected entry, including payload. Admission and result are unique; retained monitor assessment reports matched prerequisites, one evaluated result, no missing observations and no parsing errors. Completion: no intervening history-changing operation occurs between admission and query. The driver then processes all other completions and replacement work regardless of the comparison. Serial 10 shows the permitted current completion leaves the same logical entry while Storage term becomes 2 and unstable is empty; serial 11 reports empty queues and follower applied/commit 4. This confirms completion of the bounded schedule, not a general cluster agreement property. The observed preservation is consistent with the source term guard and overlay query mechanism; no mutation/counterfactual test isolates that guard as a necessary cause. Considered alternatives and checked counterarguments: A weaker entry-index-only stabilization interpretation would not distinguish the recurring entry identity from its earlier completion; the actual message-term filter is a distinct protection. The control shows current replacement completion can retire the overlay while retaining the same logical entry; the checker does not require all completions to leave unstable memory untouched. Expected and actual entries use the same serialization helper, but independent producers supply them: emitted storage work versus subsequent logical query. No expected result is copied into the observation.
limitations: One fixed five-node no-crash schedule and one correlated delayed completion; not universal coverage.
MemoryStorage substitutes device durability; crash recovery and write-error behavior are outside scope.
The verified endpoint is the local logical log entry. Commit agreement, externally visible client results and general liveness are not checked.
The final permitted completion is a recorded control, not an additional formal property.
